attributes.affiliation_basis: ADS-B is an unauthenticated cooperative broadcast: it states an identity — a callsign, an emitter category, an address — and there is no integrity mechanism beyond the CRC, which detects corruption and not forgery. UNKNOWN is therefore not the format's silence but a refusal to read a self-declared, spoofable claim as an identification
attributes.position_unavailable_reason: an ADS-B type code 2 frame carries no position fields
attributes.symbol_basis: derived from affiliation; ADS-B states no symbol
attributes.valid_from_basis: an ADS-B extended squitter carries no time field at all — not a date, not a second of the minute. The receipt instant is used, and the frame itself states nothing about when. The AVR '@' timestamp, where present, is a free-running 12 MHz receiver counter and not a wall clock, so it is parked and never read as one

payload.observed_at_basis: an ADS-B extended squitter carries no time field at all — not a date, not a second of the minute. The receipt instant is used, and the frame itself states nothing about when. The AVR '@' timestamp, where present, is a free-running 12 MHz receiver counter and not a wall clock, so it is parked and never read as one
payload.parity_basis: the frame's 24-bit parity field, 91F096, verified as the Mode S CRC of its first 88 bits. A frame that fails is refused rather than best-effort decoded
payload.received_at_basis: the injected clock. An ADS-B frame stream carries no wall-clock timestamp — the AVR '@' field is a receiver counter — so unlike AIS there is no feed-supplied delivery instant to prefer over ours
payload.severity_basis: ADS-B states no urgency outside a surveillance status of 1 and a type code 28 emergency state; INFO is the format's silence, not an assessment that nothing is wrong
